newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex to invest $800 million in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Telmex to invest $800 million in 1997.

text.p: Mexican telephone giant Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) plans to invest $800 million in 1997 to improve its network and face a host of new competitors, Telmex director general Jaime Chico Pardo said on Tuesday.

"In the coming year, we plan to invest $800 million to keep our network modern, improve services, and grow, not only in long-distance services but in all services -- rural telefony, local service, etc.," Chico Pardo told reporters.

Telmex has invested $500 million this year in making sure its competitors will be able to place long-distance calls beginning next year by connecting to Telmex's existing network, Chico Pardo said while inaugurating a switching center in this northern industrial city.
He added that since Telmex was privatized in late 1990, the formerly state-owned company has invested more than $12 billion improving Mexico's outdated phone network.

Chico Pardo acknowledged that Telmex's future competitors, which include firms backed by AT&T and MCI, are going to be tough rivals, but he said Telmex plans aggressive new services to hold onto its customers.
"We plan caller ID, voice mail, and other so-called digital services. We are also launching our own Internet service," he told reporters.
He added that Telmex received 22,000 customer complaints during the first nine months of the year, compared to 89,000 complaints during all of 1995.
"We want a good enough service so that we get no complaints at all. But they are definitely decreasing. When we were first privatized, we got hundreds of thousands of complaints per year," he said.
